title: Tech View keeps its own column choice, separate from List, for each user
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has both).
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  3. In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.
  4. At least 1 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Esther Howard") and an email.
    • Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
  5. A second browser or computer, and a second location you can switch to in the top bar (e.g. "Trailer Shop").
  6. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
  7. Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
    • On the Lines tab click New Line, enter a name (e.g. "Brake inspection") and labor hours (e.g. 2.0), and save the line.
    • Click the line's Approve (check) button so the work order status reads Approved.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders in List, open the column chooser (Columns) and write down which columns are on.
  2. Pick Tech View, open its column chooser, turn Service Advisor off and Assigned Techs on.
  3. Pick List and read whether Service Advisor and Assigned Techs changed there.
  4. In List turn Progress off.
  5. Pick Tech View and read whether Progress changed there.
  6. Log out, log back in and open Tech View.
  7. In the second browser sign in as the same user and open Tech View.
  8. Switch to the second location in the top bar and open Tech View.
  9. Open List in each of the above and read its columns.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Tech View's choice does not touch List: after step 3 List still shows Service Advisor (and has no Assigned Techs). List's choice does not touch Tech View: after step 5 Tech View still shows Progress.
  • Tech View keeps Service Advisor off and Assigned Techs on after logging back in, in the second browser and at the second location. List keeps its own columns (Progress off) exactly as it saves them today.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10048 (Story 5, Fields to display (Board View) and columns (Tech View)); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S5-R1, S5-R8, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions DR-33 (Tech View's column selection separate from List both ways). Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R1: “Tech View has its own optional-column selection, separate from List. Changing columns in Tech View never changes List, and changing columns in List never changes Tech View.”
  • S5-R8: “Save the Tech View column selection per user across logout/login, devices, and locations. List keeps saving its columns exactly as it does today.”
